cards.d: A burden is a serious or difficult responsibility.
cards.e: Children who do not behave are a burden to their parents.
cards.ielts: An ageing population places a heavy financial burden on younger workers, who must pay higher taxes to fund pensions.

cards.d: To compromise is to agree to something that is not exactly what you want.
cards.e: We both compromised about the game we decided to play.
cards.ielts: When land is limited, city planners must compromise between building new housing and preserving green spaces.

cards.d: To craft something is to make it using skill.
cards.e: She crafted the bookcase out of solid pine wood and then painted it.
cards.ielts: Local artisans in Rishtan craft beautiful ceramics by hand, using techniques that have been passed down for centuries.

cards.d: A crook is someone who is not honest or who commits crimes.
cards.e: The manager was arrested by the police for being a crook.
cards.ielts: Online crooks increasingly target elderly people with fake emails that ask for their bank details.

cards.d: Currency is the form of money used in a certain place.
cards.e: Elizabeth had to exchange her dollars for foreign currency.
cards.ielts: Travellers can now pay by card almost everywhere, so there is less need to exchange currency before a trip abroad.

cards.d: An enigma is someone or something that is mysterious or hard to understand.
cards.e: The theft of the paintings is an enigma to the investigators.
cards.ielts: How the ancient builders moved such enormous stones remains an enigma that archaeologists are still trying to solve.

cards.d: When people or things are fragile, they are not strong and can be damaged easily.
cards.e: The fragile glassware was carefully packed into boxes.
cards.ielts: Coral reefs are extremely fragile ecosystems that can be destroyed by even small increases in ocean temperature.

cards.d: A hybrid is a mixture of different things or styles.
cards.e: In Greek mythology, a centaur is a hybrid of a man and a horse.
cards.ielts: Many universities now offer a hybrid of online and face-to-face teaching, which gives students greater flexibility.

cards.d: Innocence is a lack of experience of difficult or complex things in life.
cards.e: Everyone who met her found her innocence to be charming.
cards.ielts: Some parents worry that exposure to violent online content is destroying the innocence of childhood far too early.

cards.d: To merge two things is to combine them into one whole thing.
cards.e: The storm clouds merged into one large menacing cloud that filled the sky.
cards.ielts: When two large banks merge, thousands of employees may lose their jobs as the new company closes duplicate branches.

cards.d: When something is moderate, it is not too big or too small in size or amount.
cards.e: It takes a moderate amount of patience to be around small children all day.
cards.ielts: Doctors recommend at least thirty minutes of moderate exercise, such as brisk walking, on most days of the week.

cards.d: To overwhelm is to exist in such a large amount that someone cannot deal with it.
cards.e: The amount of homework her teacher assigned has overwhelmed her.
cards.ielts: During the pandemic, hospitals in many countries were overwhelmed by the number of patients needing intensive care.

cards.d: A perception of a situation is a way of thinking about it or understanding it.
cards.e: Since he couldn’t see, his perception of life was much different than mine.
cards.ielts: Social media can distort young people’s perception of reality, making them believe that others live perfect lives.

cards.d: A reunion is the meeting of people or things that have been separated.
cards.e: Every summer we have a family reunion at the lake.
cards.ielts: Last summer, I attended a school reunion where I met classmates I had not seen for more than ten years.

cards.d: To rig something means to dishonestly arrange it.
cards.e: The bad politician rigged the election so that he would win.
cards.ielts: International observers were sent to monitor the vote after the opposition claimed that previous elections had been rigged.

cards.d: A shiver is a shaking movement the body makes when someone is cold or scared.
cards.e: I got shivers on my way home because it was so cold.
cards.ielts: I still remember the shiver of fear I felt before giving my first public speech in front of the whole school.

cards.d: When someone is sociable, they are friendly.
cards.e: Many of my good friends are sociable, but I am shy.
cards.ielts: Sociable people often thrive in jobs such as sales and tourism, where they constantly meet and talk to new customers.

cards.d: When someone is talkative, they talk a lot.
cards.e: My aunt is very talkative whenever she is on the phone.
cards.ielts: I was quite talkative as a child, so my teachers often had to remind me to stay quiet during lessons.

cards.d: To tow something is to pull it.
cards.e: The truck was towing a trailer behind it.
cards.ielts: Cars that are parked illegally in the city centre are towed away, and their owners have to pay a large fine.

cards.d: To tramp is to put your feet down in a loud, heavy way as you walk.
cards.e: The baby tramped across the floor as he was learning to walk.
cards.ielts: Thousands of hikers tramp along the popular mountain trails every summer, causing serious erosion and damage to plant life.
